title: Electric Current
notes: In a **closed circuit**, electric charges flow round without stopping. This flow of electric charges is called an **electric current**, or current for short. The charges leave the positive terminal of the cell, pass through the appliance, and return to the negative terminal. A steady current needs two things: an energy source and a complete path.

We measure current with an **ammeter**, connected in series in the circuit. Its unit is the **ampere** (A); smaller currents are measured in milliamperes (mA), where 1 mA = 0.001 A. For example, 250 mA is 250 × 0.001 = 0.25 A. The red knob (+) goes to the positive terminal of the cell and the black knob (−) to the negative terminal.

A current has two useful effects. The **heating effect**: thermal energy is given out when a current flows through a conductor, so a kettle's heating part becomes hot, and the effect grows as the current grows. The **magnetic effect**: a coil of wire carrying a current becomes an **electromagnet** and attracts paper clips. Adding a cell raises the current, which makes the bulb brighter.
callout: For a direction question, say: from the positive terminal of the cell, through the appliance, to the negative terminal. Arrows drawn the other way lose the mark.

options.text: A flow of electric charges round a closed circuit
A flow of electrical energy from a cell
The push a cell gives to the charges in a wire
The number of charges stored inside a cell

questions.why: Current is the flow of electric charges, which needs an energy source and a complete path.
questions.wrongWhy: Treating current as a flow of energy or as a push confuses it with energy transfer and with voltage. Answer: a flow of electric charges.

questions.prompt: A current of 250 mA flows through a bulb. What is this current in amperes?
questions.wrongWhy: Dividing by 10 000 gives 0.025 A, and multiplying instead of dividing gives 250 000 A; milli means thousandths. Answer: 0.25 A.

questions.prompt: A student adds one more cell, connected the same way, to a circuit with a single bulb. What happens?

options.text: The current increases and the bulb becomes brighter
The current increases but the bulb stays equally bright
The current stays the same because the bulb has not changed
The current decreases and the bulb becomes dimmer

questions.why: In Practical 8.4, adding cells in the same direction increased the current and the bulb grew brighter.
questions.wrongWhy: Cells in the same direction add energy rather than oppose each other, so the current cannot fall or stay fixed. Answer: the current increases and the bulb becomes brighter.

questions.prompt: A coil of insulated copper wire is wound round an iron nail and joined to a cell. When the switch is closed, the coil

options.text: becomes an electromagnet and attracts paper clips
becomes a permanent magnet that still attracts after the switch is opened
becomes magnetic only if the wire is made of plastic
gets hot but shows no magnetic effect at all

questions.why: A current through a coil of wire produces the magnetic effect, turning the coil into an electromagnet.
questions.wrongWhy: The magnetism lasts only while current flows, and the coil must be a conductor such as copper, not plastic. Answer: it becomes an electromagnet and attracts paper clips.
